items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Concert tour in Switzerland with the New Ragtime Band directed by a very sensitive clarinet player, Jacky Millet.

ctx.x: I did another recording for a British fellow who was trying to push a young British pianist named Mike Garret. I was told that Mike had been doing a lot of classical piano, was very talented and wanted to play jazz. We decided to record in Paris with Art Taylor on drums, Jean Francois Castoire on bass and Francois Guin, named "Frick" on trombone. We found out that Mike had never before played with an ensemble and didn't know the art of accompanying soloists. We did our best and called the album "Three Generations…

The same routine went on during most of 1969. Concert tour in Switzerland with the New Ragtime Band directed by a very sensitive clarinet player, Jacky Millet. Concerts in France, with my group with Marc Hemmler, piano, Pierre Sim, bass, and Francho Manzzechi on drums. I was giving now and then, Negro Spirituals concerts. I was part of a show with a big choral from Lyon, "the Bardanes".

It has been two years since I had not been in London again, but the occasion came for the Expo which was a week long festival, sponsored by the Harold Davison Agency and George Wain, that featured many American musicians as well as English groups, and once again, I was to meet and work with a famous musician I had heard and read plenty about but never seen.
